title: MessageType `Control` in upper case, over CBOR

source.clause: §10 Session management ("manage session states using a separate message with MessageType 'Control'"); ECMA-430 §5 ¶2, §5.1.1
source.note: composed: §10 spells the reserved value `Control` where ECMA-430 §5.1.1 spells it `control`, and §5 makes capitalization irrelevant to a field's value. The bytes are `{"MessageType": "Control", "Format": "text", "Subformat": "english", "Content": "Close the session."}` through conformance/tools/cbor_encode.py — PascalCase keys, as Annex A spells them.

notes: The casing of the *value* is not preserved by `is_control`, which compares case-insensitively, but it is preserved in the model and in canonical_json: §5 says capitalization does not change what a value means, not that an implementation may rewrite an opaque one. Only `format` is canonicalised, because Table 1 fixes its spellings.
